question: Which developmental transcription factors along with ISL1 and MEF2C shows significant motif enrichment in genes differentially expressed between ascending and descending fibroblasts?

nodes.label: Define ascending vs descending fibroblast DE gene sets and appropriate background
Select developmental transcription factor motif database and map TFs to motif IDs
Perform motif enrichment analysis on DE gene regulatory regions relative to background
Filter enriched motifs for those corresponding to developmental TFs including ISL1 and MEF2C
Apply statistical significance thresholds and multiple-testing correction to enriched developmental TF motifs
Compile list of significantly enriched developmental TFs co-enriched with ISL1 and MEF2C and interpret in fibroblast developmental context
Load fibroblast expression data, define ascending vs descending fibroblast groups, run differential expression to obtain up/down DE gene lists and extract matched genomic background gene set
Download a developmental TF-focused motif collection (e.g., JASPAR vertebrates plus cardiac/neural crest developmental TFs), and construct a TF-to-motif ID mapping table including ISL1 and MEF2C

Define regulatory regions (e.g., ±2 kb from TSS or ATAC peaks linked to DE genes), retrieve corresponding genomic sequences for DE and background genes, and run motif enrichment (e.g., HOMER, MEME-AMEn, or GimmeMotifs) comparing DE vs background regions
Annotate enriched motif results with TF IDs using the TF-to-motif mapping, then subset to motifs assigned to developmental TFs and explicitly retain entries corresponding to ISL1 and MEF2C
Apply statistical filters to developmental TF motifs (e.g., FDR q-value < 0.05 and minimum enrichment fold-change or odds ratio threshold) using multiple-testing correction across all tested motifs

From the significant developmental TF motif set, compile a list of TFs whose motifs are significantly enriched alongside ISL1 and MEF2C, and summarize their developmental roles relevant to fibroblast and aortic development
